brief: GS's positioning note reports that its CTA model expects systematic trend followers to sell a net $10bn of equities this week if prices and vols hold near current levels, with SPX an outlier forecast to buy $8.5bn under the same conditions; over the next month the model's down-tape scenario implies $184.91bn of net selling. GS Prime Brokerage data show global and US equities net bought by hedge funds, led by short covers and long buys in Info Tech and Communication Services, while Health Care was net sold for a fifth straight week at the fastest pace in nearly six months, pushing its long/short ratio to 2.32 versus a March high of 3.04. Buyback blackout is near 64% of the S&P 500 and rising toward an estimated 85% by week's end, easing progressively once October earnings season starts, Financials first. GS reiterates that earnings, not valuation re-rating, should drive further S&P 500 upside toward its 8000/8300/8700 targets, with pivot levels at 7643/7420/6944.
